title: Require Service Contract Authority
forbids: a module contract directory whose index lacks one generic exported contract anchor or at least one filename-mapped direct leaf import; contract source acquiring module implementation, router, or middleware faces; a contract leaf cycling through its own index; a direct contract leaf without exactly one filename-mapped public operation or group export; export-list aliasing except for an ECMAScript-reserved public operation name; a contract operation or group without Standard Schema adaptation at every input, output, or public error-data position; a contract or reusable DTO or error-data schema using executable, unsafe, native-only, or pre-2020-12 TypeBox capabilities; imported, computed, spread, or exported error-map authority; and an imported shorthand error item
why: A module contract directory exposes one generic native oRPC contract authority through index.ts while direct semantic leaves own one filename-mapped public operation or deliberate group. Private spelling is not public contract authority, including when an ECMAScript-reserved public key requires an export-list alias. Public input, output, and error-data schemas use TypeBox's native JSON Schema builders and one Standard Schema adapter without silently projecting away runtime semantics.
remediate: Export the generic contract only from contract/index.ts and prove at least one filename-mapped direct leaf import. Compose that acquired leaf anywhere in the plain or native nested contract tree; TypeScript owns completeness, Knip owns import reachability, and generated client/API behavior proof owns the complete public operation set. Keep contract source independent of module implementation, router, and middleware faces, and keep leaves independent of their own index. Give each kebab-case leaf exactly one lower-camel public runtime export mapped from its filename. For an ECMAScript-reserved public operation, export any private local binding under that filename-mapped name and import the public name under any valid private binding. Remove executable, unsafe, native-only, and tuple capabilities from public schemas, and apply standard(TypeBoxSchema) at every input, output, and public error-data position. Declare public errors with an inline or private local object-literal .errors map, keep shorthand error items private and local, and use the handler-supplied errors constructors in procedures.
message: Service module contract directories must preserve one generic entrypoint and declarative TypeBox/native error authority in their leaves.
